newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU condemns hostage-taking in Peru.
newsitem.headline: EU condemns hostage-taking in Peru.

text.p: The European Union (EU) condemned the taking hostage of the Japanese ambassador and his guests, including several EU diplomats and citizens, in Lima, Peru.

In a statement issued by EU president Ireland late on Wednesday, the 15-nation bloc urged those responsible to release unharmed and without delay all hostages still detained on property protected by international law.

Heavily-armed guerrillas of the Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) interrupted a party to commemorate the Japanese emperor's birthday on Tuesday, taking at least 200 people captive at the ambassador's residence.
They are demanding the release of 400 to 500 jailed comrades and the presence of Peru's president Alberto Fujimori for talks.
The hostages include many high-ranking diplomats, businessmen and government officials.
The EU said it felt sure that the Peruvian government would do everything to protect the lives of the hostages. REUTER JOS
